I need a channel beam with 70mm width, 40mm height, a length 450mm with a wall thickness of 5mm, which is open on the top side | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept – step-by-step (no functions executed yet)

1. Choose a coordinate system  
   • X-axis: channel width (70 mm)  
   • Y-axis: channel length (450 mm)  
   • Z-axis: channel height (40 mm – measured upward from the underside)

2. Build the outer solid (first block, NOT a subtraction)  
   • x_size = 70, y_size = 450, z_size = 40  
   • basepoint (x,y,z) = (0, 0, 0)  
   • subtraction = False (establishes the initial volume)

3. Carve out the interior to create the U-shape (second block, subtraction = True)  
   • Wall thickness required on every closed side = 5 mm  
   • Therefore the void’s cross-section is:  
     – width: 70 − 2·5 = 60 mm  
     – height: 40 − 5 = 35 mm (bottom still 5 mm thick, top completely open)  
     – length remains 450 mm  
   • Void block’s basepoint:  
     – x = 5 (leaves 5 mm side wall on both sides)  
     – y = 0 (full length)  
     – z = 5 (leaves 5 mm bottom wall)  
   • subtraction = True (removes this volume from the outer solid)

4. Confirm geometry creation is finished by calling the finished function with allFunctionsCalled = true.

The complete sequence therefore requires exactly two block-function calls (outer solid + interior subtraction) followed by one finished-function call.

When you are ready for me to prepare the actual function calls, just let me know.
